purpose: Executable baseline for familiar local-library workflows. Action counts exclude typing and playback time.

coverage.desktop: covered by mocked Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit journeys

tasks.expected: Movies and TV are direct visible destinations; neither requires a promotional row or hosted sign-in.
Switching between Movies and TV keeps each profile's saved view and sort choice.
Folder hierarchy, back navigation, and folder scroll restoration require named libraries and folder browsing.
tasks.evidence: Issues #40 and #114 own the implementation and acceptance.

tasks.expected: Search is reachable from the visible header and accepts a local title query.
Open then close details restores focus to the originating library card and preserves its rail position.
A saved per-profile view and sort are returned after the local database is reopened.
Selecting a local title resumes through the existing playback flow.
Audio-track controls (#30) and captions/subtitles (#31) remain visible in-player controls when delivered.
tasks.evidence: Issues #30 and #31 own their respective implementation and acceptance.

tasks.expected: Episode continuation returns predictably to the prior series context when delivered.
tasks.evidence: Issue #29 owns the implementation and acceptance.

tasks.expected: Profiles can hide/reorder home sections and keep optional recommendations from displacing local-library access after upgrades.
tasks.evidence: Issue #83 owns the implementation and acceptance.

tasks.expected: Slow, missing, and corrupt artwork never blocks usable browsing; reduced-motion behavior remains usable.
tasks.evidence: Issue #56 owns the artwork/splash implementation and targeted tests.
